recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which identity you use on the numerator and how you get two standard limits out of x².

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use the sum-to-product identity
steps.margin_note: First mark. Watch the order: cos C − cos D = 2 sin((C + D)/2) sin((D − C)/2), so the second sine takes D minus C, not C minus D. That order fixes the sign of the answer.
lines: At x = 0 the numerator is 1 − 1 = 0 and x² = 0, so the form is 0/0.
Use  cos C − cos D = 2 sin((C + D)/2) · sin((D − C)/2)  with C = ax and D = bx.
∴ cos ax − cos bx = 2 sin((a + b)x/2) · sin((b − a)x/2)

recall.must_convey: That cos C − cos D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) sin((D−C)/2) is applied, giving 2 sin((a+b)x/2) sin((b−a)x/2).
accept: use cos c minus cos d equals two sin half sum into sin d minus c by two
the numerator becomes two sin a plus b x by two into sin b minus a x by two
apply the sum to product formula for cosines
cos c minus cos d formula vaadali, rendu sines vasthayi
convert the difference of cosines into a product of two sines

steps.why: The numerator has to become a product of two factors, each of order x, before it can be matched against x². Each sine then supplies one power of x.
common_mistakes: Writing sin((C − D)/2) instead of sin((D − C)/2), which reverses the sign of the answer.
Using the sin C − sin D identity, which produces a cosine and only one sine.
steps.memory_tip: For cosines the identity gives two sines. Keep the order of the question: cos ax comes first, so the second bracket is (b − a)x/2.

steps.label: Apply lim sin θ / θ = 1 twice
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Split x² as x · x and give one x to each sine. Each bracket then needs its own half-angle coefficient outside.
lines: Write x² = x · x and give one x to each sine.
Each bracketed quotient tends to 1 as x → 0, so

recall.must_convey: That each sine is matched with its own angle to give 1, leaving 2 · ((a+b)/2) · ((b−a)/2) = (b² − a²)/2.
accept: each sine over its own angle is one so the answer is b squared minus a squared by two
the constants left are a plus b by two and b minus a by two
the answer is b square minus a square over two
b square minus a square by two vasthundi
split x squared as x into x and use sin theta by theta twice

steps.why: Each sine contributes one power of x, so x² is exactly used up and a finite value is left. The order of the answer checks against a simple case: putting a = 0 gives (1 − cos bx)/x² = b²/2, and (b² − 0)/2 = b²/2. Numerically, with a = 3 and b = 5 the value is 8, matching (25 − 9)/2.
common_mistakes: Giving (a² − b²)/2, the correct size with the wrong sign.
Forgetting the half-angle coefficients and answering 2(a + b)(b − a).
steps.memory_tip: The alternative route gives the same check: (cos ax − 1)/x² → −a²/2 and (1 − cos bx)/x² → b²/2, and adding them gives (b² − a²)/2.

insider_note: cos C − cos D turns the top into a product of two sines, and x² splits as x · x to feed one to each. The answer (b² − a²)/2 has b first — the order comes from (D − C)/2.
